transcript.message:
Hi Maya — thanks for taking my 30-minute consult. I’m Alex: visiting Rome for a week, obsessed with local food, and I want a truly authentic dinner (less touristy, local atmosphere, Roman classics done right). I’m ready to book a reservation for one of your two recommendations, and I’ll choose at the end of our call.

Before you propose the two restaurants, quick clarifying questions so your suggestions hit the mark:

1. Dates & time
- My trip is a week-long but I haven’t locked a specific night yet. Do you need an exact date? I’m aiming for a dinner around 8–9pm on one night this week — how far in advance should I book each place?

2. Party size
- I’ll be dining for 2 (me + one guest). Can you give recommendations that suit two people?

3. Budget
- Comfortable with roughly €60–€120 per person (food + a glass or two of wine). If authentic spots you recommend typically cost more/less, tell me the expected price range.

4. Food preferences & restrictions
- I love Roman classics (cacio e pepe, carbonara, amatriciana) and’m open to seasonal or offal dishes if they’re traditional. No allergies. If a restaurant is better for vegetarians or has no seafood, please flag that.

5. Ambiance & location
- Priority: authentic, local, not tourist-trap. Prefer an intimate neighborhood trattoria or family-run osteria — also open to a lively enoteca. I’ll be staying centrally (near Pantheon/Trastevere) — ideally within a 20–30 minute taxi/transport ride. If one option is trastevere/centro and another in a quieter neighborhood, that’s fine.

6. Booking help
- Can you (a) make the reservation for me, or (b) provide exact phone number/email/booking link and step-by-step tips? I’d prefer you handle the booking if you can, but if not, I’ll call/book.

When you give the two restaurant options, please include for each:
- Short description (why it’s authentic / why locals go)
- Signature dishes I should order (and one insider ordering tip)
- Typical price per person (range) including wine
- Neighborhood & exact address (and approximate travel time from Pantheon)
- Reservation info: phone, website/booking link, typical lead time, cancellation policy if known
- Atmosphere (quiet/romantic/lively), dress code, outdoor seating availability
- Any dietary/vegetarian accommodations
- A quick pro/con compared to the other option
- If you can make the booking, say so and tell me what info you need from me (date/time, full name, phone, email, credit card if required).

Once I have those two options I’ll choose one and confirm — then ask you to make/create the reservation if possible. Ready when you are.

1) Dates & time / lead time
- Do I need an exact date? Only if we’re booking a table. If you’re flexible, we can pick the best-fit night based on your week’s plan.
- Lead time:
  - Trattoria da Enzo al 29: no reservations (walk-in); the “lead time” is showing up early and queuing. Important note: it’s lunch-only (12:30–15:00), so it won’t work for an 8–9pm dinner.
  - Ristorante Colosseo Vista: reservations recommended; for 8–9pm I’d book 3–7 days ahead (earlier if you want rooftop/sunset).

2) Party size
- Both suit 2 people well. Enzo is tight/cramped (part of the charm), Colosseo Vista is more spacious and polished.

3) Budget (typical spend with 1–2 glasses of wine)
- Trattoria da Enzo al 29: roughly €25–€40 per person (very budget-friendly versus your range).
- Ristorante Colosseo Vista: roughly €70–€110 per person (fits your stated comfort zone).

4) Food preferences
- Both will cover Roman classics like carbonara/cacio e pepe.
- If you want truly traditional/offal: Enzo is the stronger match (e.g., trippa alla romana).

5) Location
- Trattoria da Enzo al 29: Trastevere (great for local atmosphere; very close to where you’re staying).
- Ristorante Colosseo Vista: Monti/Colosseum area (central, but heavily touristed).

6) Booking help
- I can’t place the reservation on your behalf directly right now, but I can give you the exact contact details and a quick step-by-step script to book efficiently.

Option 1: Trattoria da Enzo al 29
- Why it’s authentic / why locals go:
  A tiny, family-run Roman trattoria in Trastevere serving classic recipes unchanged for decades; it’s lively, no-frills, and very local in spirit (including the queue and tight tables).
- Signature dishes + insider ordering tip:
  - Order: Cacio e pepe, Carbonara, Trippa alla romana (if you’re game), Carciofi alla giudia (when available).
  - Insider tip: Don’t over-order—portions are satisfying and the kitchen is fast; also don’t ask for parmesan on seafood pasta (classic Roman etiquette).
- Typical price per person (with wine):
  ~€25–€40 pp.
- Neighborhood/address + travel time from Pantheon:
  Via dei Vascellari 29, Trastevere. About 10–15 min by taxi from the Pantheon (or ~25 min on foot).
- Reservation info / lead time / cancellation:
  - Reservations: not required and generally not offered; walk-ins only.
  - Phone: +39 06 581 2260 (useful to confirm they’re open, but expect walk-in service).
  - Hours: Mon–Sat 12:30–15:00; closed Sunday. (So: lunch only.)
  - Cancellation: not applicable (no booking).
- Atmosphere:
  Lively, loud, very cramped; casual dress; some outdoor seating.
- Dietary/vegetarian:
  Vegetarian options exist, but it’s not designed for strict vegan/gluten-free dining (and detailed allergen info isn’t formalized).
- Pro vs con (compared to Colosseo Vista):
  - Pro: far more “real Rome” and less touristy; stronger traditional cooking.
  - Con: cannot do dinner; expect a wait; cash only.

Option 2: Ristorante Colosseo Vista
- Why people go:
  Rooftop terrace with panoramic Colosseum views, designed for a “special night out” experience rather than a neighborhood trattoria vibe.
- Signature dishes + insider ordering tip:
  - Order: Carbonara, Tiramisu (and a cocktail if you want the full experience).
  - Insider tip: Book rooftop timing explicitly (especially if you want sunset), and follow the smart-casual dress expectation to avoid seating limitations.
- Typical price per person (with wine):
  ~€70–€110 pp.
- Neighborhood/address + travel time from Pantheon:
  Via dei Fori Imperiali 42, Monti. About 10–15 min by taxi from the Pantheon (or ~20–25 min by transit/walk depending on route).
- Reservation info / lead time / cancellation:
  - Booking link: https://www.colosseovista.it/reservations
  - Website: https://www.colosseovista.it
  - Phone: +39 06 678 4521
  - Lead time: 3–7 days recommended for prime 8–9pm rooftop slots.
  - Cancellation policy: not confirmed here—check during booking flow.
- Atmosphere:
  Elegant/romantic, moderate noise; smart-casual; rooftop/outdoor seating available; very photo-friendly.
- Dietary/vegetarian:
  Stronger for dietary needs (vegetarian/vegan/gluten-free available; detailed allergen guidance).
- Pro vs con (compared to Enzo):
  - Pro: easy to reserve, dinner-friendly, great view, good for dietary flexibility.
  - Con: much more touristed and “occasion dining” than local trattoria culture.

Given your stated top priority (authentic, local, not tourist-trap, Roman classics done right), I’d steer you to the Trastevere trattoria experience—even though it means shifting this from dinner to lunch.

I recommend Trattoria da Enzo al 29.
